reviews.summary: A major Binance hot-wallet compromise from Oct. 29 remains under remediation, with ETH among impacted assets and withdrawals only being restored in phases. This creates current ETH market/venue-operational uncertainty.
materialRisks: Binance reported approximately $6.3B in stolen token assets from compromised hot wallets on Oct. 29, including ETH; the investigation and remediation remain ongoing.
Binance had suspended withdrawals for security review and is restoring them progressively, creating near-term venue/liquidity and market-dislocation risk for ETH.

facts.fact: Binance’s Oct. 30 official update says hot wallets were compromised around 20:05 UTC on Oct. 29, with roughly $6.3B of token assets affected, including ETH; it stated that the full attack sequence was still under investigation.
Binance said withdrawals were temporarily suspended during security checks, with restoration planned in phases rather than fully completed immediately.
Binance stated it was covering losses with SAFU/corporate funds and actively sourcing remaining affected assets through market and OTC channels, which may add short-term flow uncertainty.
Ethereum Foundation’s latest Glamsterdam announcement schedules only Sepolia activation; Ethereum mainnet activation remains TBD, so no imminent mainnet upgrade date was identified.
